verdicts.reason: The claim is right and was already hand-confirmed (verified-by-review.md 'Confirmed WRONG' #1). E-2 has no `countries`, and the engine shows it OPEN to a UZ reader with a bachelor's. The proposed group is ad hoc, though. It has SA but no other Arabic-speaking country, ES but no Latin America, DE but not AT/CH. It also leaves out India: Indian nationals can teach English on E-2 under the Korea–India CEPA, as I recall (not re-checked this session). A 7-country-only gate would be wrong the other way, because it blocks Russian citizens teaching Russian, a legal route that matters for this site's readers. The rule ties the language to the reader's own nationality, which the engine cannot express. So the list has to be a deliberate allow-list, with a note for the non-English members.

F-4 has a manual-documented `change` list. Its early-adaptation exemption for '3+ years on a long-term status' presupposes applicants already in Korea on long-term statuses, and the repo's exceptions restrict only short-term (B/C) sources. The new edges should therefore carry that condition as a note rather than be bare.

verdicts.reason: The claim is right: F-5-11 has no needs, age, countries or lang, and the engine shows it OPEN to every reader from E-1/E-3/E-6-1/E-6-3/E-7-1/F-2-7/NONE. The legal basis is 'outstanding ability recognised by the Minister' across science, business, education, arts and sport. The fix is wrong. A visa-level `needs: {edu: 5}` is not the legal test, and in a simulation it BLOCKS an E-6-3 athlete or E-6-1 artist who answered high school. Those are exactly the arts and sport groups the decree names. The engine has no fact for 'outstanding achievement', so the honest fix is wording, not a gate: no visa needs, and a clearer `how` (shown on every move, because these moves carry no note).
